source.text: בֶּן־שָׁנָ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתֵּ֣י שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of [...] year[s was] Saul in his reigning, and two years he reigned over Israel.

en.L: Saul [was] [...] years old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel.
en.B: Saul was ... years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel two years.
en.R: Saul was ... years old when he became king. He ruled over Israel for two years.

es.L: Saúl [tenía] [...] años cuando comenzó a reinar, y reinó dos años sobre Israel.
es.B: Saúl tenía ... años cuando llegó a ser rey, y reinó sobre Israel dos años.
es.R: Saúl tenía ... años cuando llegó a ser rey. Gobernó sobre Israel durante dos años.

fr.L: Saül [avait] [...] ans quand il devint roi, et il régna deux ans sur Israël.
fr.B: Saül avait ... ans quand il devint roi, et il régna deux ans sur Israël.
fr.R: Saül avait ... ans quand il est devenu roi. Il a régné sur Israël pendant deux ans.

vi.L: Sau-lơ [được] [...] tuổi khi lên làm vua, và ông cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên hai năm.
vi.B: Sau-lơ được ... tuổi khi lên làm vua, và ông cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên hai năm.
vi.R: Sau-lơ được ... tuổi khi lên làm vua. Ông cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên hai năm.

decisions.choice: Saul's age is missing from the Hebrew text; the gap is shown, not filled
alternatives: thirty years old (a few later Greek manuscripts)
one year old, read as a year into his reign (an old Jewish reading)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Saul was a son of a year when he became king", which is the usual way of giving a king's age (2 Samuel 2:10; 5:4), but the number itself is missing, since Saul already has a grown son in verse 2. A number seems to have dropped out when the text was copied. The verse is missing from the main early manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation, and a few later Greek manuscripts read "thirty years old", which looks like a later attempt to fill the gap. No surviving text gives a reading that can be trusted, so the translation marks the gap. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: he reigned two years: the number is kept as the Hebrew gives it, though part of it may be lost
decisions.reason: Saul's reign covers many events from here to 1 Samuel 31, and Acts 13:21 speaks of forty years for Saul. So many think a tens figure has dropped out before "two" (for example twenty-two or forty-two). Others take "two years" as the time until the events that follow, or until his rejection. The Hebrew number is kept, and the question stays open.

decisions.choice: the opening formula for a king's reign
decisions.reason: This is the pattern the books of Samuel and Kings use to begin the account of a reign: the king's age when he became king and the length of his reign (2 Samuel 2:10; 5:4; 1 Kings 14:21). Here it begins the story of Saul's rule after his public crowning in 11:15.

decisions.choice: [...] at Literal; ... at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Every level marks the missing number the same way, so that no level supplies an age the Hebrew does not give (m1). The footnote tells the reader why.

source.text: וַיִּבְחַר־ל֨וֹ שָׁא֜וּל שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֮ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיִּהְי֨וּ עִם־שָׁא֜וּל אַלְפַּ֗יִם בְּמִכְמָשׂ֙ וּבְהַ֣ר בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְאֶ֗לֶף הָיוּ֙ עִם־י֣וֹנָתָ֔ן בְּגִבְעַ֖ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וְיֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם שִׁלַּ֖ח אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And chose for himself Saul 3,000 from Israel, and were with Saul 2,000 in Michmash and in [the] hill country of Bethel, and 1,000 were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin; and [the] rest of the people he sent away, each to his tents.

en.L: And Saul chose for himself 3,000 from Israel; 2,000 were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and 1,000 were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, each to his tents.
en.B: Saul chose 3,000 men of Israel for himself. Of these, 2,000 stayed with Saul in Michmash and the hill country of Bethel, and 1,000 were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent home, each to his own tent.
en.R: Saul chose 3,000 men from Israel to be his army. He kept 2,000 of them with him at Michmash and in the hills around Bethel. The other 1,000 were with Jonathan, Saul's son, at Gibeah in the land of Benjamin. Saul sent all the rest of the men back home.

es.L: Y Saúl escogió para sí 3 000 de Israel; 2 000 estaban con Saúl en Micmas y en la región montañosa de Betel, y 1 000 estaban con Jonatán en Guibeá de Benjamín. Y al resto del pueblo lo despidió, cada uno a sus tiendas.
es.B: Saúl escogió para sí 3 000 hombres de Israel. De ellos, 2 000 se quedaron con Saúl en Micmas y en la región montañosa de Betel, y 1 000 estaban con Jonatán en Guibeá de Benjamín. Al resto del pueblo lo mandó a casa, cada uno a su tienda.
es.R: Saúl escogió 3 000 hombres de Israel para que fueran su ejército. Se quedó con 2 000 de ellos en Micmas y en las colinas de Betel. Los otros 1 000 estaban con Jonatán, el hijo de Saúl, en Guibeá, en la tierra de Benjamín. Saúl mandó de vuelta a casa a todos los demás hombres.

fr.L: Et Saül se choisit trois mille [hommes] d’Israël : deux mille étaient avec Saül à Mikmash et dans la montagne de Béthel, et mille étaient avec Jonathan à Guibea de Benjamin. Et le reste du peuple, il le renvoya chacun à ses tentes.
fr.B: Saül choisit pour lui trois mille hommes d’Israël. Deux mille restèrent avec Saül à Mikmash et dans la montagne de Béthel, et mille étaient avec Jonathan à Guibea de Benjamin. Il renvoya le reste du peuple, chacun dans sa tente.
fr.R: Saül a choisi trois mille hommes d’Israël pour former son armée. Il en a gardé deux mille avec lui à Mikmash et dans les collines autour de Béthel. Les mille autres étaient avec Jonathan, le fils de Saül, à Guibea, dans le pays de Benjamin. Saül a renvoyé tous les autres hommes chez eux.

vi.L: Sau-lơ chọn cho mình ba nghìn người từ Y-sơ-ra-ên: hai nghìn người ở với Sau-lơ tại Mích-ma và trong miền đồi núi Bê-tên, còn một nghìn người ở với Giô-na-than tại Ghi-bê-a thuộc Bên-gia-min. Phần dân còn lại thì ông cho về, ai về trại nấy.
vi.B: Sau-lơ chọn cho mình ba nghìn người Y-sơ-ra-ên. Trong số đó, hai nghìn người ở với Sau-lơ tại Mích-ma và miền đồi núi Bê-tên, còn một nghìn người ở với Giô-na-than tại Ghi-bê-a thuộc Bên-gia-min. Số dân còn lại ông cho về nhà.
vi.R: Sau-lơ chọn ba nghìn người Y-sơ-ra-ên làm quân đội của mình. Ông giữ hai nghìn người với mình tại Mích-ma và vùng đồi núi quanh Bê-tên. Một nghìn người kia ở với Giô-na-than, con trai Sau-lơ, tại Ghi-bê-a trong đất Bên-gia-min. Sau-lơ cho tất cả những người còn lại về nhà.

decisions.choice: Saul forms a standing force of chosen men
decisions.reason: Until now Israel's fighting men gathered only when called out and went home afterward (11:7-8). Saul keeps 3,000 picked men on duty and sends the rest of the large army from 11:8 home. This is what Samuel had warned a king would do (8:11-12).

decisions.choice: Michmash, Bethel, Gibeah: towns in the hill country north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Michmash lay a few miles north of Gibeah across a deep valley; Bethel was a little to the north and west of it. Gibeah of Benjamin was Saul's home town (10:26; 11:4). The places set the scene for the fighting in this chapter and the next.

decisions.choice: each to his tents: home
decisions.reason: "To his tents" is an old way of saying "home", from the time when Israel lived in tents. It does not mean the men were living in tents in the field.

decisions.choice: men; to be his army
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives only the numbers. Balanced adds "men", and Readable says why Saul chose them (m1).

decisions.choice: Jonathan, Saul's son
decisions.reason: Jonathan appears here for the first time without introduction. Verse 16 calls him Saul's son, and Readable says so at once so young readers can follow.

decisions.choice: "Mikmash", "Jonathan"
decisions.reason: "Jonathan" is the Samuel terms note's form; "Mikmash" transcribes the town's name with k and sh, as "Ashdod" and "Ishbosheth" in the note. Numbers are written out in words, as French running text writes them.

decisions.choice: "Jonatán", "Micmas", "Geba", "Bet-avén", "Ofra", "Sual", "Bet-horón", "el valle de Zeboim"
decisions.reason: Names follow the Samuel terms note ("Jonatán") and otherwise their usual Spanish form, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "Giô-na-than", "Mích-ma"
decisions.reason: "Giô-na-than" as the Samuel terms note; "Mích-ma" the usual transliteration, kept through chapters 13-14.

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ יוֹנָתָ֗ן אֵ֣ת נְצִ֤יב פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגֶ֔בַע וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְשָׁאוּל֩ תָּקַ֨ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֤ר בְּכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשְׁמְע֖וּ הָעִבְרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck Jonathan [the] garrison of [the] Philistines that [was] in Geba, and heard [the] Philistines; and Saul blew on the trumpet in all the land, saying, let hear the Hebrews.

en.L: And Jonathan struck the garrison of [the] Philistines that [was] in Geba, and [the] Philistines heard. And Saul blew the trumpet in all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
en.B: Jonathan attacked the Philistine garrison at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Then Saul blew the ram's horn throughout the land and said, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
en.R: Jonathan attacked the Philistine soldiers who were stationed at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Then Saul had the trumpet blown all through the land. He said, "Let all the Hebrews hear about this!"

es.L: Y Jonatán atacó la guarnición de [los] filisteos que [estaba] en Geba, y [los] filisteos lo oyeron. Y Saúl tocó la trompeta por toda la tierra, diciendo: «¡Que lo oigan los hebreos!».
es.B: Jonatán atacó la guarnición filistea de Geba, y los filisteos se enteraron. Entonces Saúl hizo sonar el cuerno de carnero por todo el país y dijo: «¡Que lo oigan los hebreos!».
es.R: Jonatán atacó a los soldados filisteos que estaban en Geba, y los filisteos se enteraron. Entonces Saúl mandó tocar la trompeta por todo el país. Dijo: «¡Que todos los hebreos se enteren de esto!».

fr.L: Et Jonathan frappa le poste des Philistins qui [était] à Guéba, et les Philistins l’apprirent. Et Saül sonna du cor dans tout le pays, en disant : « Que les Hébreux entendent ! »
fr.B: Jonathan attaqua le poste philistin de Guéba, et les Philistins l’apprirent. Saül fit alors sonner le cor de bélier dans tout le pays, en disant : « Que les Hébreux l’entendent ! »
fr.R: Jonathan a attaqué les soldats philistins qui étaient installés à Guéba, et les Philistins l’ont appris. Alors Saül a fait sonner la trompette dans tout le pays. Il a dit : « Que tous les Hébreux l’apprennent ! »

vi.L: Giô-na-than đánh đồn binh của người Phi-li-tin tại Ghê-ba, và người Phi-li-tin nghe [tin ấy]. Sau-lơ thổi kèn khắp xứ mà nói: "Hãy để người Hê-bơ-rơ nghe!"
vi.B: Giô-na-than tấn công đồn binh Phi-li-tin tại Ghê-ba, và người Phi-li-tin nghe tin ấy. Bấy giờ Sau-lơ cho thổi kèn sừng dê đực khắp xứ và nói: "Hãy cho người Hê-bơ-rơ nghe!"
vi.R: Giô-na-than tấn công toán quân Phi-li-tin đóng ở Ghê-ba, và người Phi-li-tin nghe tin ấy. Bấy giờ Sau-lơ cho thổi kèn khắp xứ. Ông nói: "Hãy cho tất cả người Hê-bơ-rơ nghe tin này!"

decisions.choice: garrison: a post of Philistine soldiers
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to set up, station". It can name a body of troops placed somewhere, an officer or governor put in charge, or a standing pillar set up as a sign of rule. Here an outpost of soldiers holding Israel down fits best. A Philistine post at "the hill of God" was mentioned in 10:5.

decisions.choice: the trumpet: the shofar, a ram's horn blown to call men to arms
decisions.reason: The instrument was a ram's horn, not a metal trumpet. Blowing it through the land was the signal to gather for war (Judges 3:27; 6:34).

decisions.choice: the Hebrews: the name others used for Israel
alternatives: the slaves have revolted (ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: "Hebrews" is the name by which foreigners, here the Philistines, usually call the Israelites (4:6, 9; 13:19; 14:11). Saul's use of it is unusual; it may echo the Philistines' word, or it may reach out to Hebrews who were not yet with Israel (14:21). The ancient Greek translation has "the slaves have revolted" here, reading similar Hebrew letters differently. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: ram's horn
decisions.reason: As in Judges 3:27, the shofar is "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and "ram's horn" at Balanced.

decisions.choice: had the trumpet blown
decisions.reason: A signal "in all the land" was carried by many horn blowers, so Readable says Saul had it blown. The other levels keep "Saul blew", which a reader can take in the same way.

decisions.choice: "trompeta" (L, R); "cuerno de carnero" (B)
decisions.reason: As the English decision: the shofar (m2) is "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and "ram's horn" at Balanced, which says what it was.

decisions.choice: "kèn sừng dê đực" (B); "kèn" (L, R) for the shofar
decisions.reason: The ram's horn (meaning decision), named at Balanced as the English names it; Literal and Readable say "trumpet".

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל שָׁמְע֣וּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־נְצִ֣יב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְגַם־נִבְאַשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיִּצָּעֲק֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אַחֲרֵ֥י שָׁא֖וּל הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel heard, saying, struck Saul [the] garrison of [the] Philistines, and also became odious Israel with the Philistines; and were called out the people after Saul [to] the Gilgal.

en.L: And all Israel heard, saying, "Saul has struck the garrison of [the] Philistines, and also Israel has become a stench to the Philistines." And the people were called out after Saul [to] Gilgal.
en.B: All Israel heard the news: "Saul has attacked the Philistine garrison, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines." And the people were called out to join Saul at Gilgal.
en.R: News spread through all Israel: "Saul has attacked the Philistine soldiers, and now the Philistines hate Israel." So the army was called together to follow Saul at Gilgal.

es.L: Y todo Israel oyó decir: «Saúl ha atacado la guarnición de [los] filisteos, y también Israel se ha hecho odioso a los filisteos». Y el pueblo fue convocado en pos de Saúl [en] Gilgal.
es.B: Todo Israel oyó la noticia: «Saúl ha atacado la guarnición filistea, y ahora Israel se ha vuelto odioso para los filisteos». Y el pueblo fue convocado para unirse a Saúl en Gilgal.
es.R: La noticia se extendió por todo Israel: «Saúl ha atacado a los soldados filisteos, y ahora los filisteos odian a Israel». Así que el ejército fue convocado para seguir a Saúl en Gilgal.

fr.L: Et tout Israël entendit dire : « Saül a frappé le poste des Philistins, et aussi Israël s’est rendu odieux aux Philistins. » Et le peuple fut convoqué à la suite de Saül à Guilgal.
fr.B: Tout Israël apprit la nouvelle : « Saül a attaqué le poste des Philistins, et maintenant Israël s’est rendu odieux aux Philistins. » Le peuple fut alors appelé à rejoindre Saül à Guilgal.
fr.R: La nouvelle s’est répandue dans tout Israël : « Saül a attaqué les soldats philistins, et maintenant les Philistins détestent Israël. » Alors on a appelé l’armée à rejoindre Saül à Guilgal.

vi.L: Cả Y-sơ-ra-ên nghe nói: "Sau-lơ đã đánh đồn binh của người Phi-li-tin, và Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng đã trở nên đáng ghê tởm đối với người Phi-li-tin." Dân chúng được triệu tập theo Sau-lơ [tại] Ghinh-ganh.
vi.B: Cả Y-sơ-ra-ên nghe tin: "Sau-lơ đã tấn công đồn binh Phi-li-tin, và bây giờ Y-sơ-ra-ên đã trở nên đáng ghê tởm đối với người Phi-li-tin." Rồi dân chúng được triệu tập theo Sau-lơ tại Ghinh-ganh.
vi.R: Tin lan ra khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Sau-lơ đã tấn công quân Phi-li-tin, và bây giờ người Phi-li-tin căm ghét Y-sơ-ra-ên." Vì vậy quân đội được triệu tập để theo Sau-lơ tại Ghinh-ganh.

decisions.choice: Saul has struck: the king is credited with his son's attack
decisions.reason: Verse 3 says Jonathan made the attack. The report gives the credit to Saul as king and leader of the army, as a commander's name is often given for what his men do.

decisions.choice: Israel has become a stench to the Philistines: the Philistines now loathe Israel and will strike back
decisions.reason: The verb means "to stink". To become a bad smell to someone is a picture for becoming hateful to them, so that they want revenge (Genesis 34:30; 2 Samuel 10:6). Israel can no longer hope to be left alone.

decisions.choice: Gilgal: the place near the Jordan where Saul was made king
decisions.reason: Gilgal lay in the Jordan valley near Jericho. Samuel had told Saul to go down there and wait for him (10:8), and the people had renewed the kingdom there (11:14-15). Calling the army there sets up the test of the next verses.

decisions.choice: the Philistines hate Israel
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the bad smell by its meaning (m2).

source.text: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים נֶאֶסְפ֣וּ׀לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֤לֶף רֶ֨כֶב֙ וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ פָּרָשִׁ֔ים וְעָ֕ם כַּח֛וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־שְׂפַֽת־הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְמִכְמָ֔שׂ קִדְמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] Philistines gathered to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariot[s] and 6,000 horsemen, and people like the sand that [is] on [the] shore of the sea for multitude; and they came up and camped in Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

en.L: And [the] Philistines gathered to fight with Israel, 30,000 chariots and 6,000 horsemen, and people like the sand that [is] on the shore of the sea for multitude. And they came up and camped in Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
en.B: The Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: 30,000 chariots, 6,000 horsemen, and foot soldiers as many as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
en.R: The Philistines gathered their army to fight against Israel. They had 30,000 chariots and 6,000 men on horses. Their foot soldiers were as many as the grains of sand on the beach. They came up and set up camp at Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven.

es.L: Y [los] filisteos se reunieron para pelear contra Israel, 30 000 carros y 6 000 jinetes, y pueblo como la arena que [está] a la orilla del mar en multitud. Y subieron y acamparon en Micmas, al oriente de Bet-avén.
es.B: Los filisteos se reunieron para pelear contra Israel: 30 000 carros, 6 000 jinetes y soldados de a pie tan numerosos como la arena de la orilla del mar. Subieron y acamparon en Micmas, al oriente de Bet-avén.
es.R: Los filisteos reunieron su ejército para pelear contra Israel. Tenían 30 000 carros de guerra y 6 000 hombres a caballo. Sus soldados de a pie eran tantos como los granos de arena de la playa. Subieron y acamparon en Micmas, al oriente de Bet-avén.

fr.L: Et les Philistins se rassemblèrent pour combattre Israël : trente mille chars et six mille cavaliers, et un peuple nombreux comme le sable qui [est] au bord de la mer. Et ils montèrent et campèrent à Mikmash, à l’orient de Beth-Aven.
fr.B: Les Philistins se rassemblèrent pour combattre Israël : trente mille chars, six mille cavaliers et des fantassins aussi nombreux que le sable au bord de la mer. Ils montèrent camper à Mikmash, à l’est de Beth-Aven.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont rassemblé leur armée pour combattre Israël. Ils avaient trente mille chars et six mille cavaliers. Leurs soldats à pied étaient aussi nombreux que les grains de sable sur la plage. Ils sont montés et ont installé leur camp à Mikmash, à l’est de Beth-Aven.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin tập họp để đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên: ba mươi nghìn chiến xa và sáu nghìn kỵ binh, và dân đông như cát trên bờ biển. Chúng đi lên đóng trại tại Mích-ma, phía đông Bết-A-ven.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin tập họp để đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên: ba mươi nghìn chiến xa, sáu nghìn kỵ binh, và bộ binh đông như cát trên bờ biển. Chúng kéo lên đóng trại tại Mích-ma, phía đông Bết-A-ven.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin tập họp quân đội để đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên. Chúng có ba mươi nghìn chiến xa và sáu nghìn kỵ binh. Bộ binh của chúng đông như cát trên bãi biển. Chúng kéo lên đóng trại tại Mích-ma, phía đông Bết-A-ven.

decisions.choice: 30,000 chariots, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: 3,000 chariots (some Greek manuscripts and the Syriac)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has thirty thousand chariots. Some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation and the Syriac translation have 3,000, which fits better beside 6,000 horsemen and with the size of chariot forces known from that time. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: like the sand on the seashore: too many to count
decisions.reason: The picture is a common one for a huge number (Genesis 22:17; Joshua 11:4; Judges 7:12). It stresses how badly Israel is outnumbered.

decisions.choice: Michmash: the place Saul had held
decisions.reason: The Philistines take over the very position where Saul's 2,000 men had been (verse 2), so Saul has fallen back to Gilgal. Beth-aven lay near Bethel (Joshua 7:2).

decisions.choice: foot soldiers
decisions.reason: "People" here means the mass of the army, set beside the chariots and horsemen, so Balanced and Readable call them foot soldiers.

source.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל רָאוּ֙ כִּ֣י צַר־ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִגַּ֖שׂ הָעָ֑ם וַיִּֽתְחַבְּא֣וּ הָעָ֗ם בַּמְּעָר֤וֹת וּבַֽחֲוָחִים֙ וּבַסְּלָעִ֔ים וּבַצְּרִחִ֖ים וּבַבֹּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] men of Israel saw that [it was] tight for him, for was hard pressed the people; and hid themselves the people in the caves and in the thickets and in the rocks and in the holes and in the pits.

en.L: And [the] men of Israel saw that it [was] tight for them, for the people were hard pressed; and the people hid themselves in the caves and in the thickets and in the rocks and in the holes and in the cisterns.
en.B: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble, because the army was hard pressed, the people hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, in holes in the ground, and in cisterns.
en.R: The men of Israel saw that they were in great danger. The enemy was pressing hard on their army. So the people hid in caves and in thick bushes. They hid among the rocks, in holes in the ground, and in pits dug to store water.

es.L: Y [los] hombres de Israel vieron que [estaban] en aprieto, porque el pueblo estaba acosado; y el pueblo se escondió en las cuevas, y en los matorrales, y en las peñas, y en los hoyos, y en las cisternas.
es.B: Cuando los hombres de Israel vieron que estaban en apuros, porque el ejército se veía acosado, la gente se escondió en cuevas y matorrales, entre las peñas, en hoyos en la tierra y en cisternas.
es.R: Los hombres de Israel vieron que estaban en gran peligro. El enemigo presionaba con fuerza a su ejército. Así que la gente se escondió en cuevas y en matorrales espesos. Se escondieron entre las rocas, en hoyos en la tierra y en pozos hechos para guardar agua.

fr.L: Et les hommes d’Israël virent qu’ils [étaient] à l’étroit, car le peuple était serré de près ; et le peuple se cacha dans les cavernes, et dans les buissons, et dans les rochers, et dans les trous, et dans les citernes.
fr.B: Quand les hommes d’Israël virent qu’ils étaient en danger, parce que l’armée était serrée de près, le peuple se cacha dans les cavernes et les fourrés, parmi les rochers, dans des trous et dans des citernes.
fr.R: Les hommes d’Israël ont vu qu’ils étaient en grand danger. L’ennemi attaquait leur armée de près. Alors les gens se sont cachés dans des grottes et dans des buissons épais. Ils se sont cachés parmi les rochers, dans des trous dans le sol et dans des fosses creusées pour garder l’eau.

vi.L: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy mình [lâm vào] cảnh ngặt nghèo, vì dân bị dồn ép; dân chúng ẩn núp trong các hang động, trong bụi rậm, trong các khe đá, trong các hầm và trong các hố chứa nước.
vi.B: Khi người Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy mình lâm nguy, vì quân đội bị dồn ép, dân chúng trốn trong hang động, trong bụi rậm, giữa các khe đá, trong hầm hố và trong các bể chứa nước.
vi.R: Người Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy mình đang lâm nguy. Quân thù dồn ép quân đội của họ. Vì vậy dân chúng trốn trong hang động và trong bụi rậm. Họ trốn giữa các tảng đá, trong hầm dưới đất, và trong những hố đào để chứa nước.

decisions.choice: it was tight for them: they were in distress
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says it was "narrow" or "tight" for them, a common picture for being trapped and in trouble.

decisions.choice: holes: underground hiding places
decisions.reason: The word is rare. In Judges 9:46, 49 a related word names an inner room or vault of a tower. Here it seems to mean dug-out places or chambers in the ground, perhaps old tombs. The exact sense is not certain, but the list as a whole means every kind of hiding place.

decisions.choice: cisterns: pits cut in the rock to store rainwater
decisions.reason: Cisterns were common in the hill country, where there were few springs. An empty one could hide a person (Genesis 37:24).

decisions.choice: the enemy was pressing hard on their army
decisions.reason: Readable names who was pressing the army, the Philistines of verse 5.

records.literal_gloss: And Hebrews crossed the Jordan [to the] land of Gad and Gilead; and Saul still he [was] in the Gilgal, and all the people trembled after him.

en.L: And Hebrews crossed the Jordan [to the] land of Gad and Gilead. And Saul [was] still in Gilgal, and all the people trembled after him.
en.B: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the troops who followed him were trembling.
en.R: Some of the Hebrews even crossed the Jordan River into the lands of Gad and Gilead. But Saul stayed at Gilgal. All the men who were with him were shaking with fear.

es.L: Y unos hebreos cruzaron el Jordán [a la] tierra de Gad y de Galaad. Y Saúl [estaba] todavía en Gilgal, y todo el pueblo temblaba en pos de él.
es.B: Algunos hebreos llegaron a cruzar el Jordán hacia la tierra de Gad y de Galaad. Pero Saúl seguía en Gilgal, y toda la tropa que lo seguía estaba temblando.
es.R: Algunos hebreos hasta cruzaron el río Jordán y se fueron a las tierras de Gad y de Galaad. Pero Saúl se quedó en Gilgal. Todos los hombres que estaban con él temblaban de miedo.

fr.L: Et des Hébreux passèrent le Jourdain [vers] le pays de Gad et de Galaad. Et Saül [était] encore à Guilgal, et tout le peuple tremblait derrière lui.
fr.B: Des Hébreux passèrent même le Jourdain pour aller dans le pays de Gad et de Galaad. Saül était toujours à Guilgal, et tous les soldats qui le suivaient tremblaient.
fr.R: Certains Hébreux ont même traversé le Jourdain pour aller dans le pays de Gad et de Galaad. Mais Saül est resté à Guilgal. Tous les hommes qui étaient avec lui tremblaient de peur.

vi.L: Có những người Hê-bơ-rơ qua sông Giô-đanh [đến] đất Gát và Ga-la-át. Còn Sau-lơ vẫn [ở] tại Ghinh-ganh, và toàn dân run sợ theo ông.
vi.B: Một số người Hê-bơ-rơ thậm chí đã vượt sông Giô-đanh sang đất Gát và Ga-la-át. Nhưng Sau-lơ vẫn ở Ghinh-ganh, và toàn quân theo ông đều run sợ.
vi.R: Một số người Hê-bơ-rơ còn vượt sông Giô-đanh sang vùng đất của Gát và Ga-la-át. Nhưng Sau-lơ vẫn ở lại Ghinh-ganh. Tất cả những người theo ông đều run sợ.

decisions.choice: Hebrews crossed: a play on words
decisions.reason: "Hebrews" and "crossed" sound alike in Hebrew (*'ivrim* and *'averu*). The Hebrews "cross over" in flight to the land east of the Jordan. The word may also point to people who were not part of Saul's army, as in 14:21; the text does not settle whether these are Israelites fleeing or another group.

decisions.choice: trembled after him: followed him trembling
decisions.reason: "After him" means following him as their leader. The men who stayed with Saul did so in fear.

decisions.choice: Gad and Gilead: Israelite land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gad was one of the tribes settled east of the Jordan, and Gilead was the hill country there (Numbers 32:1, 33). It lay out of the Philistines' reach.

decisions.choice: Some Hebrews even crossed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no article on "Hebrews", so it means some of them, not all. "Even" shows that this goes further than the hiding in verse 6.

decisions.choice: "Giô-đanh", "Gát" (the tribe of Gad, as the published Genesis) and "Ga-la-át"
decisions.reason: The published forms; the tribe of Gad and the Philistine city Gath are both "Gát" in Vietnamese, and "đất Gát và Ga-la-át" east of the Jordan leaves no doubt here.

records.literal_gloss: And he waited seven days, for the appointed time that Samuel [had set], and not came Samuel [to] the Gilgal, and was scattering the people from with him.

en.L: And he waited seven days, according to the appointed time that Samuel [had set], but Samuel did not come [to] Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
en.B: He waited seven days, the time Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to slip away from Saul.
en.R: Saul waited seven days, as Samuel had told him to. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the men began to leave Saul and go away.

es.L: Y esperó siete días, conforme al plazo que Samuel [había fijado], pero Samuel no vino [a] Gilgal, y el pueblo se le dispersaba.
es.B: Esperó siete días, el plazo que Samuel había fijado, pero Samuel no llegaba a Gilgal, y la tropa empezó a abandonar a Saúl.
es.R: Saúl esperó siete días, como Samuel le había dicho. Pero Samuel no llegaba a Gilgal, y los hombres empezaron a dejar a Saúl y a irse.

fr.L: Et il attendit sept jours, selon le temps fixé que Samuel [avait indiqué], mais Samuel ne vint pas à Guilgal, et le peuple se dispersait loin de lui.
fr.B: Il attendit sept jours, le délai fixé par Samuel, mais Samuel ne vint pas à Guilgal, et les soldats commencèrent à abandonner Saül.
fr.R: Saül a attendu sept jours, comme Samuel le lui avait dit. Mais Samuel n’est pas venu à Guilgal, et les hommes ont commencé à quitter Saül pour s’en aller.

vi.L: Ông đợi bảy ngày, theo thời hạn Sa-mu-ên [đã định], nhưng Sa-mu-ên không đến Ghinh-ganh, và dân chúng tản mác khỏi ông.
vi.B: Ông đợi bảy ngày theo thời hạn Sa-mu-ên đã định, nhưng Sa-mu-ên không đến Ghinh-ganh, và quân lính bắt đầu bỏ Sau-lơ mà đi.
vi.R: Sau-lơ đợi bảy ngày như Sa-mu-ên đã dặn. Nhưng Sa-mu-ên không đến Ghinh-ganh, và quân lính bắt đầu bỏ Sau-lơ mà đi.

decisions.choice: the appointed time: the seven days Samuel set in 10:8
decisions.reason: Samuel had told Saul, "You shall go down before me to Gilgal ... seven days you shall wait until I come to you and show you what you are to do" (10:8). Saul keeps the seven days, but not to the end of the last one (verses 10-11).

decisions.choice: that Samuel [had set]: the verb is not written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the appointed time that Samuel", leaving out a verb such as "set" or "said". The sense is clear from 10:8. The written Hebrew letters and the reading tradition also differ slightly in the form of "he waited", without changing the meaning.

decisions.choice: the people were scattering: men were deserting
decisions.reason: The verb pictures the army breaking up and going off in all directions. Each day of waiting cost Saul men, which is the pressure he names in verse 11.

decisions.choice: slip away (Balanced); leave Saul and go away (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is ongoing, so Balanced and Readable say the men "began" to leave.

en.B: So Saul said, "Bring the burnt offering and the peace offerings here to me." Then he offered the burnt offering.
en.R: So Saul said, "Bring me the animals for the burnt offering and the peace offerings." Then he offered the burnt offering.

es.L: Y Saúl dijo: «{{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} el holocausto y los sacrificios de paz». Y ofreció el holocausto.
es.B: Entonces Saúl dijo: «{{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} aquí el holocausto y los sacrificios de paz». Y ofreció el holocausto.
es.R: Entonces Saúl dijo: «{{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} los animales para el holocausto y los sacrificios de paz». Luego ofreció el holocausto.

fr.L: Et Saül dit : « Amenez-moi l’holocauste et les sacrifices de communion. » Et il offrit l’holocauste.
fr.B: Saül dit donc : « Amenez-moi l’holocauste et les sacrifices de communion. » Puis il offrit l’holocauste.
fr.R: Alors Saül a dit : « Apportez-moi les animaux pour le sacrifice complet par le feu et pour les sacrifices de communion. » Puis il a offert le sacrifice complet par le feu.

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói: "Hãy đem đến cho ta tế lễ thiêu và các tế lễ bình an." Rồi ông dâng tế lễ thiêu.
vi.B: Vậy Sau-lơ nói: "Hãy đem tế lễ thiêu và các tế lễ bình an đến cho ta." Rồi ông dâng tế lễ thiêu.
vi.R: Vậy Sau-lơ nói: "Hãy đem các con vật dùng làm tế lễ thiêu và tế lễ bình an đến cho ta." Rồi ông dâng tế lễ thiêu.

decisions.choice: burnt offering and peace offerings: sacrifices to seek the LORD's help before battle
decisions.reason: The burnt offering was burned whole for the LORD; the peace offerings were shared in a meal. Samuel had offered a burnt offering before battle in 7:9, and he had promised to come to Gilgal to offer both kinds (10:8).

decisions.choice: he offered up the burnt offering: Saul does what Samuel had said he would come to do
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Saul handled the sacrifice himself or had it done for him. Samuel's rebuke in verse 13 is not about who may offer but about Saul not keeping the command to wait (10:8).

decisions.choice: the animals for
decisions.reason: What was brought to Saul were the animals to be offered, so Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the king says "ta" to his men
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: the king says "ta" and "ngươi"; Saul speaks so from his crowning.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְהַעֲל֣וֹת הָעֹלָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל בָּ֑א וַיֵּצֵ֥א שָׁא֛וּל לִקְרָאת֖וֹ לְבָרֲכֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as he finished to offer up the burnt offering, and look, Samuel coming; and went out Saul to meet him, to bless him.

en.L: And it was, as he finished offering up the burnt offering, look, Samuel was coming. And Saul went out to meet him, to bless him.
en.B: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to meet him and greet him.
en.R: Saul had just finished offering the burnt offering when Samuel arrived. Saul went out to meet him and welcome him.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando acababa de ofrecer el holocausto, he aquí que Samuel venía. Y Saúl salió a su encuentro para bendecirlo.
es.B: Justo cuando terminaba de ofrecer el holocausto, llegó Samuel. Saúl salió a su encuentro para saludarlo.
es.R: Saúl acababa de ofrecer el holocausto cuando llegó Samuel. Saúl salió a recibirlo y a darle la bienvenida.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme il achevait d’offrir l’holocauste, que voici, Samuel arrivait. Et Saül sortit à sa rencontre pour le bénir.
fr.B: Au moment même où il achevait d’offrir l’holocauste, Samuel arriva. Saül sortit à sa rencontre pour le saluer.
fr.R: Saül venait juste de finir d’offrir le sacrifice quand Samuel est arrivé. Saül est sorti à sa rencontre pour l’accueillir.

vi.L: Khi ông vừa dâng xong tế lễ thiêu, kìa, Sa-mu-ên đến. Sau-lơ ra đón người để chào mừng người.
vi.B: Ông vừa dâng xong tế lễ thiêu thì Sa-mu-ên đến. Sau-lơ ra đón và chào mừng người.
vi.R: Sau-lơ vừa dâng xong tế lễ thiêu thì Sa-mu-ên đến. Sau-lơ ra đón và chào mừng người.

decisions.choice: look, Samuel was coming: Samuel arrives at that very moment
decisions.reason: The word "look" draws the reader into the scene: Samuel comes the moment the offering is done, not after a long delay. Saul had waited almost long enough.

decisions.choice: to bless him: to greet him
decisions.reason: "Bless" is often used of a greeting, wishing someone well when meeting (25:14; 2 Kings 4:29).

decisions.choice: greet (Balanced); welcome (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the everyday word for the meaning of "bless" here (m2).

decisions.choice: and you, you did not come: Saul puts weight on Samuel's delay
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "you" to the verb, which gives it stress. Saul names three pressures (the men leaving, Samuel's absence, the Philistines' gathering) and lays part of the blame on Samuel.

decisions.choice: at the appointed time of the days: within the seven days Samuel set
decisions.reason: This points back to the seven days of verse 8 and 10:8. Saul claims Samuel had not come within them, though Samuel arrives just as the offering ends (verse 10).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Saul's sentence runs on into verse 12 ("... I said"), so Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma. Readable breaks it into short sentences.

decisions.choice: Samuel and Saul go on saying "ông" and "tôi" to each other
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: the prophet who anointed him is not his subject, and Saul does not use "ta" with Samuel.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר עַ֠תָּה יֵרְד֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֵלַי֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א חִלִּ֑יתִי וָֽאֶתְאַפַּ֔ק וָאַעֲלֶ֖ה הָעֹלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and I said, now will come down [the] Philistines to me [to] the Gilgal, and [the] face of Yahweh not I have entreated; and I forced myself and offered up the burnt offering.

en.L: and I said, 'Now [the] Philistines will come down against me [to] Gilgal, and I have not entreated the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},' and I forced myself, and I offered up the burnt offering."
en.B: I thought, 'The Philistines will now come down on me at Gilgal, and I have not yet sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s favor.' So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering."
en.R: I thought, 'The Philistines are about to come down and attack me here at Gilgal, and I have not yet asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to help us.' So I felt I had to offer the burnt offering."

es.L: y dije: “Ahora [los] filisteos bajarán contra mí [a] Gilgal, y no he implorado el rostro {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”, y me esforcé, y ofrecí el holocausto».
es.B: y pensé: “Ahora los filisteos van a bajar contra mí a Gilgal, y todavía no he buscado el favor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”. Así que me vi obligado a ofrecer el holocausto».
es.R: Pensé: “Los filisteos están a punto de bajar a atacarme aquí en Gilgal, y todavía no le he pedido {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} que nos ayude”. Así que sentí que tenía que ofrecer el holocausto».

fr.L: et je me suis dit : “Maintenant, les Philistins vont descendre contre moi à Guilgal, et je n’ai pas apaisé la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}” ; et je me suis fait violence, et j’ai offert l’holocauste. »
fr.B: Je me suis dit : “Les Philistins vont maintenant descendre m’attaquer à Guilgal, et je n’ai pas encore cherché la faveur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.” Alors je me suis fait violence et j’ai offert l’holocauste. »
fr.R: Je me suis dit : “Les Philistins vont bientôt descendre m’attaquer ici, à Guilgal, et je n’ai pas encore demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} de nous aider.” Alors j’ai pensé que je devais offrir le sacrifice. »

vi.L: thì tôi nói: 'Bây giờ người Phi-li-tin sẽ xuống đánh tôi [tại] Ghinh-ganh, mà tôi chưa nài xin ơn trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}},' nên tôi đành phải dâng tế lễ thiêu."
vi.B: nên tôi nghĩ: 'Bây giờ người Phi-li-tin sẽ xuống đánh tôi tại Ghinh-ganh, mà tôi chưa cầu xin ơn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.' Vì vậy tôi đành phải dâng tế lễ thiêu."
vi.R: Tôi nghĩ: 'Người Phi-li-tin sắp xuống tấn công tôi ở Ghinh-ganh, mà tôi chưa cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ chúng ta.' Vì vậy tôi thấy mình phải dâng tế lễ thiêu."

decisions.choice: entreated the face of the LORD: asked for the LORD's favor and help
decisions.reason: The phrase means to soften someone's face, that is, to appeal to them for kindness. It is used of praying to God for mercy or help (Exodus 32:11; 1 Kings 13:6). Saul would not go to battle without first seeking the LORD.

decisions.choice: I forced myself: I made myself do it against my own reluctance
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold oneself in or to compel oneself (Genesis 43:31; Esther 5:10). Saul presents the offering as something he did unwillingly, under pressure.

decisions.choice: I said: I said to myself, I thought
decisions.reason: "Said" here is Saul's own reasoning, not words spoken to anyone.

decisions.choice: I thought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "I said" here (m3).

decisions.choice: asked the LORD to help us
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom of m1 into plain words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל נִסְכָּ֑לְתָּ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗רְתָּ אֶת־מִצְוַ֞ת יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ךְ כִּ֣י עַתָּ֗ה הֵכִ֨ין יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־מַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Samuel to Saul, you have acted foolishly; not you have kept [the] commandment of Yahweh your God that he commanded you; for now would have established Yahweh your kingdom over Israel until forever.

en.L: And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded you; for now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
en.B: Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you. Had you kept it, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would now have made your kingdom over Israel secure for all time.
en.R: Samuel said to Saul, "You have done a foolish thing. You did not obey the command {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you. If you had obeyed, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would have let you and your sons after you rule over Israel forever.

es.L: Y Samuel dijo a Saúl: «Has obrado neciamente. No has guardado el mandamiento {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tu Dios que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te mandó; porque ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habría confirmado tu reino sobre Israel para siempre.
es.B: Samuel le dijo a Saúl: «Has actuado como un necio. No has cumplido el mandamiento que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dio. Si lo hubieras cumplido, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habría afirmado ahora tu reino sobre Israel para siempre.
es.R: Samuel le dijo a Saúl: «Has hecho una tontería. No obedeciste la orden que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dio. Si hubieras obedecido, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habría dejado que tú y tus hijos después de ti gobernaran sobre Israel para siempre.

fr.L: Et Samuel dit à Saül : « Tu as agi follement. Tu n’as pas gardé le commandement {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’avait ordonné ; car maintenant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aurait affermi ta royauté sur Israël pour toujours.
fr.B: Samuel dit à Saül : « Tu as agi en insensé. Tu n’as pas observé le commandement que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’avait donné. Si tu l’avais observé, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aurait maintenant affermi pour toujours ta royauté sur Israël.
fr.R: Samuel a dit à Saül : « Tu as fait une folie. Tu n’as pas obéi à l’ordre que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’avait donné. Si tu avais obéi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous aurait laissés régner sur Israël pour toujours, toi et tes fils après toi.

vi.L: Sa-mu-ên nói với Sau-lơ: "Ông đã hành động dại dột. Ông đã không giữ điều răn của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ông mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã truyền cho ông; vì lẽ ra bây giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững vương quốc ông trên Y-sơ-ra-ên đến đời đời.
vi.B: Sa-mu-ên nói với Sau-lơ: "Ông đã hành động dại dột. Ông đã không giữ điều răn mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ông truyền cho ông. Nếu ông đã giữ, thì bây giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững vương quốc ông trên Y-sơ-ra-ên đến đời đời.
vi.R: Sa-mu-ên nói với Sau-lơ: "Ông đã làm một việc dại dột. Ông đã không vâng theo mệnh lệnh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ông truyền cho ông. Nếu ông vâng lời, thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho ông và con cháu ông cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên mãi mãi.

decisions.choice: you have acted foolishly: a moral and spiritual failure, not a lack of cleverness
decisions.reason: In the Bible the fool is someone who acts without regard for God. Saul later uses the same word of himself (26:21), and David does after his census (2 Samuel 24:10).

decisions.choice: the commandment: the order to wait at Gilgal for Samuel (10:8)
decisions.reason: The command Saul broke is the one Samuel gave in the LORD's name when he anointed him: wait seven days until I come and show you what to do.

decisions.choice: for now the LORD would have established: what would have happened had Saul obeyed
alternatives: If only you had kept the commandment ...
decisions.reason: The words describe what was possible but is now lost. Some have suggested reading "if only" for "not" at the start of the sentence ("If only you had kept ..."), which differs in Hebrew by one letter, but the sense of the whole is the same either way.

decisions.choice: your kingdom forever: a lasting royal line
decisions.reason: A kingdom established "forever" means rule passed on to the king's descendants, as the LORD later promises David (2 Samuel 7:16). Saul's disobedience costs his family the throne, not yet his own reign.

decisions.choice: Had you kept it (Balanced); If you had obeyed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that what follows is what would have happened (m3).

decisions.choice: let you and your sons after you rule
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a kingdom established forever means (m4).

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה מַמְלַכְתְּךָ֣ לֹא־תָק֑וּם בִּקֵּשׁ֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ כִּלְבָב֗וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ יְהוָ֤ה לְנָגִיד֙ עַל־עַמּ֔וֹ כִּ֚י לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶֽׁר־צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: But now your kingdom not will stand; has sought Yahweh for himself a man according to his heart, and has appointed him Yahweh as ruler over his people, for not you have kept what commanded you Yahweh.

en.L: But now your kingdom will not stand. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sought for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} a man according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has appointed him as ruler over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, because you have not kept what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you."
en.B: But now your kingdom will not last. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has looked for a man after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own heart, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has appointed him ruler over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, because you have not kept what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you."
en.R: But now your kingdom will not last. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has looked for a man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen, one who shares what is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has already appointed that man to be the leader of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. This is because you did not obey what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you."

es.L: Pero ahora tu reino no permanecerá. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se ha buscado un hombre conforme a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha designado como gobernante sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, porque no has guardado lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te mandó».
es.B: Pero ahora tu reino no durará. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha buscado un hombre conforme a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio corazón, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha nombrado gobernante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, porque no has cumplido lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te mandó».
es.R: Pero ahora tu reino no va a durar. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha buscado un hombre escogido por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, uno que comparte lo que hay en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} corazón. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ya ha nombrado a ese hombre como líder de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo. Esto es porque no obedeciste lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te mandó».

fr.L: Mais maintenant, ta royauté ne tiendra pas. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est cherché un homme selon {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} cœur, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a établi chef sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, parce que tu n’as pas gardé ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’avait ordonné. »
fr.B: Mais maintenant, ta royauté ne durera pas. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est cherché un homme selon {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} cœur, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a établi comme chef de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, parce que tu n’as pas observé ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’avait ordonné. »
fr.R: Mais maintenant, ton règne ne durera pas. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a cherché un homme qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi, quelqu’un qui partage ce qui est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} cœur. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a déjà désigné cet homme pour être le chef de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple. C’est parce que tu n’as pas obéi à ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’avait ordonné. »

vi.L: Nhưng bây giờ vương quốc ông sẽ không đứng vững. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã tìm cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một người theo lòng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập người ấy làm người lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì ông đã không giữ điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền cho ông."
vi.B: Nhưng bây giờ vương quốc ông sẽ không bền lâu. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã tìm được một người theo lòng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập người ấy làm người lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì ông đã không giữ điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền cho ông."
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ vương quốc ông sẽ không bền lâu. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã tìm được một người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chọn, một người có cùng tấm lòng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập người ấy làm lãnh đạo dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Đó là vì ông đã không vâng theo điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền cho ông."

decisions.choice: a man according to his heart: a man of the LORD's own choosing, who shares his purposes
decisions.reason: "According to his heart" can mean "as he wishes, of his own choice" (compare 14:7, "according to your heart") and also suggests a man whose heart is set the same way as the LORD's. Both senses are present: the LORD chooses the new king, and he is one who will obey. Paul quotes this verse of David in Acts 13:22.

decisions.choice: has sought, has appointed: the choice is already made
decisions.reason: The verbs speak of the LORD's choice as already done, though David is not anointed until 16:13. What the LORD has decided is as good as done.

decisions.choice: ruler: the one the LORD sets over his people
decisions.reason: The word was used of Saul himself when he was anointed (9:16; 10:1). It names a leader appointed by the LORD to rule his people for him.

decisions.choice: a man he has chosen, one who shares what is in his heart
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both sides of the idiom (m1). Its "already" brings out m2.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: The word for ruler is "leader" at Readable, as in the terms used for these books.

decisions.choice: "một người theo lòng Ngài" (L, B)
decisions.reason: A man of the LORD's own choosing who shares his purposes (meaning decision); "theo lòng Ngài" keeps the Hebrew picture without reducing it to "pleasing", and Readable spells it out as the English does.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל וַיַּ֛עַל מִן־הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל גִּבְעַ֣ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל אֶת־הָעָם֙ הַנִּמְצְאִ֣ים עִמּ֔וֹ כְּשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Samuel and went up from the Gilgal [to] Gibeah of Benjamin; and mustered Saul the people found with him, about 600 men.

en.L: And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal [to] Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people found with him, about 600 men.
en.B: Then Samuel got up and went from Gilgal up to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the troops who were still with him, about 600 men.
en.R: Then Samuel left Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin. Saul counted the men who were still with him. There were only about 600 of them.

es.L: Y Samuel se levantó y subió de Gilgal [a] Guibeá de Benjamín. Y Saúl pasó revista al pueblo que se hallaba con él, unos 600 hombres.
es.B: Luego Samuel se levantó y subió de Gilgal a Guibeá de Benjamín. Saúl contó la tropa que aún estaba con él: unos 600 hombres.
es.R: Después Samuel salió de Gilgal y subió a Guibeá, en la tierra de Benjamín. Saúl contó los hombres que todavía estaban con él. Solo eran unos 600.

fr.L: Et Samuel se leva et monta de Guilgal à Guibea de Benjamin. Et Saül passa en revue le peuple qui se trouvait avec lui, environ six cents hommes.
fr.B: Puis Samuel se leva et monta de Guilgal à Guibea de Benjamin. Saül passa en revue les soldats qui étaient encore avec lui : environ six cents hommes.
fr.R: Ensuite, Samuel a quitté Guilgal et il est monté à Guibea, dans le pays de Benjamin. Saül a compté les hommes qui étaient encore avec lui. Il n’y en avait plus qu’environ six cents.

vi.L: Sa-mu-ên đứng dậy, từ Ghinh-ganh đi lên Ghi-bê-a thuộc Bên-gia-min. Sau-lơ kiểm điểm dân chúng còn ở với mình, được khoảng sáu trăm người.
vi.B: Rồi Sa-mu-ên đứng dậy rời Ghinh-ganh đi lên Ghi-bê-a thuộc Bên-gia-min. Sau-lơ kiểm điểm quân lính còn ở với mình, được khoảng sáu trăm người.
vi.R: Rồi Sa-mu-ên rời Ghinh-ganh đi lên Ghi-bê-a trong đất Bên-gia-min. Sau-lơ đếm số người còn ở với mình. Chỉ còn khoảng sáu trăm người.

decisions.choice: Samuel goes up to Gibeah, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: Samuel went on his way; the rest of the people went up after Saul from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin (ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads more here: "Samuel arose and went away from Gilgal on his way. And the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the men of war, and they came from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin." This explains how Saul came to be in Geba of Benjamin (verse 16). A copyist's eye may have jumped from the first "from Gilgal" to the second, leaving the words out of the Hebrew. The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: mustered: counted the men fit to fight
decisions.reason: The verb is used of counting and ordering troops. Of the 3,000 men Saul had chosen and the people called to Gilgal (verses 2, 4), only about 600 remain (14:2).

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable shows how few men were left, in line with m2.

source.text: וְשָׁא֞וּל וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְהָעָם֙ הַנִּמְצָ֣א עִמָּ֔ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים בְּגֶ֣בַע בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים חָנ֥וּ בְמִכְמָֽשׂ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people found with them [were] staying in Geba of Benjamin, and [the] Philistines camped in Michmash.

en.L: And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people found with them [were] staying in Geba of Benjamin, and [the] Philistines camped in Michmash.
en.B: Saul and his son Jonathan and the troops who were with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines were camped at Michmash.
en.R: Saul, his son Jonathan, and the men with them stayed at Geba in the land of Benjamin. The Philistines were camped at Michmash.

es.L: Y Saúl y Jonatán su hijo y el pueblo que se hallaba con ellos [estaban] en Geba de Benjamín, y [los] filisteos acamparon en Micmas.
es.B: Saúl, su hijo Jonatán y la tropa que estaba con ellos se quedaron en Geba de Benjamín, mientras los filisteos acampaban en Micmas.
es.R: Saúl, su hijo Jonatán y los hombres que estaban con ellos se quedaron en Geba, en la tierra de Benjamín. Los filisteos estaban acampados en Micmas.

fr.L: Et Saül et Jonathan son fils et le peuple qui se trouvait avec eux demeuraient à Guéba de Benjamin, et les Philistins campaient à Mikmash.
fr.B: Saül, son fils Jonathan et les soldats qui étaient avec eux s’étaient installés à Guéba de Benjamin, tandis que les Philistins campaient à Mikmash.
fr.R: Saül, son fils Jonathan et les hommes qui étaient avec eux sont restés à Guéba, dans le pays de Benjamin. Les Philistins campaient à Mikmash.

vi.L: Sau-lơ, Giô-na-than con trai ông và dân chúng còn ở với họ [đang] ở tại Ghê-ba thuộc Bên-gia-min, còn người Phi-li-tin đóng trại tại Mích-ma.
vi.B: Sau-lơ, con trai ông là Giô-na-than, và quân lính ở với họ đóng tại Ghê-ba thuộc Bên-gia-min, còn người Phi-li-tin đóng trại tại Mích-ma.
vi.R: Sau-lơ, con trai ông là Giô-na-than, và những người theo họ ở lại Ghê-ba trong đất Bên-gia-min. Người Phi-li-tin thì đóng trại tại Mích-ma.

decisions.choice: Geba and Michmash: two camps facing each other across a ravine
decisions.reason: Geba stood on the south side of a deep, steep-sided valley and Michmash on the north (14:4-5). The two armies could see each other across it.

decisions.choice: Geba of Benjamin: a town near Gibeah, not the same place
decisions.reason: Geba and Gibeah both come from the word for "hill" and lay close together in Benjamin, so they are easy to confuse (compare verses 2-3, 15). Here Saul has moved to Geba, where Jonathan had attacked the Philistine post (verse 3).

decisions.choice: in the land of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Readable explains "of Benjamin" as the tribal land, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "Ghê-ba" for Geba, kept apart from "Ghi-bê-a" (Gibeah)
decisions.reason: Two nearby towns, not the same place (meaning decision); the Vietnamese forms keep them distinct.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֧א הַמַּשְׁחִ֛ית מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֑ים הָרֹ֨אשׁ אֶחָ֥ד יִפְנֶ֛ה אֶל־דֶּ֥רֶךְ עָפְרָ֖ה אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ שׁוּעָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And came out the destroyer from [the] camp of [the] Philistines [in] three companies; the company one turned to [the] road [to] Ophrah, to [the] land of Shual.

en.L: And the raiders came out from the camp of [the] Philistines [in] three companies. The one company turned toward [the] road [to] Ophrah, to [the] land of Shual.
en.B: Raiding parties came out of the Philistine camp in three companies. One company turned toward the road to Ophrah, in the land of Shual.
en.R: Groups of raiders went out from the Philistine camp. There were three groups. One group took the road to Ophrah, in the area of Shual.

es.L: Y los saqueadores salieron del campamento de [los] filisteos [en] tres compañías. Una compañía se dirigió [por el] camino [de] Ofra, hacia [la] tierra de Sual.
es.B: Del campamento filisteo salieron tropas de saqueo en tres compañías. Una compañía tomó el camino de Ofra, en la tierra de Sual.
es.R: Del campamento filisteo salieron grupos de saqueadores. Eran tres grupos. Uno de ellos tomó el camino de Ofra, en la zona de Sual.

fr.L: Et les dévastateurs sortirent du camp des Philistins [en] trois corps : un corps prit la route d’Ophra, vers le pays de Shoual,
fr.B: Des troupes de pillards sortirent du camp des Philistins en trois corps. L’un prit la route d’Ophra, dans le pays de Shoual.
fr.R: Des groupes de pillards sont sortis du camp des Philistins. Il y avait trois groupes. Un groupe a pris la route d’Ophra, dans la région de Shoual.

vi.L: Toán quân cướp phá từ trại Phi-li-tin kéo ra [chia làm] ba đội. Một đội rẽ về hướng đường [đi] Óp-ra, đến đất Su-anh.
vi.B: Các toán quân cướp phá từ trại Phi-li-tin kéo ra thành ba đội. Một đội rẽ về hướng đường đi Óp-ra, trong đất Su-anh.
vi.R: Các toán quân cướp phá từ trại Phi-li-tin kéo ra. Có ba toán. Một toán đi theo đường về Óp-ra, trong vùng Su-anh.

decisions.choice: the raiders: a force sent out to destroy and plunder
decisions.reason: The word means "the destroyer", used here for a body of troops whose task was to ravage the land. The same word is used of the destroying power in Egypt (Exodus 12:23). The raids were meant to strip Israel's countryside and wear down its people, not to fight Saul's army.

decisions.choice: companies: divisions of the force
decisions.reason: The word is "heads", used of the separate bands into which an army was divided (Judges 7:16; 9:43).

decisions.choice: Ophrah, the land of Shual: to the north
decisions.reason: This Ophrah was a town of Benjamin (Joshua 18:23), north of Michmash. The land of Shual is otherwise unknown. Each of the three companies takes a different direction (verse 18), spreading the raids over the whole region.

source.text: וְהָרֹ֤אשׁ אֶחָד֙ יִפְנֶ֔ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית חֹר֑וֹן וְהָרֹ֨אשׁ אֶחָ֤ד יִפְנֶה֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַגְּב֔וּל הַנִּשְׁקָ֛ף עַל־גֵּ֥י הַצְּבֹעִ֖ים הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the company one turned [to the] road [to] Beth-horon, and the company one turned [to the] road [to] the border that looks down over [the] valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

en.L: And the one company turned [to the] road [to] Beth-horon, and the one company turned [to the] road [to] the border that looks down over the valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
en.B: Another company turned toward the road to Beth-horon, and another turned toward the road to the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
en.R: Another group went toward Beth-horon. The third group went toward the border area that looks down over the Valley of Zeboim, facing the desert.

es.L: Y otra compañía se dirigió [por el] camino [de] Bet-horón, y otra compañía se dirigió [por el] camino de la frontera que mira hacia el valle de Zeboim, hacia el desierto.
es.B: Otra compañía tomó el camino de Bet-horón, y otra el camino de la frontera que domina el valle de Zeboim, hacia el desierto.
es.R: Otro grupo fue hacia Bet-horón. El tercer grupo fue hacia la zona de la frontera que mira hacia el valle de Zeboim, frente al desierto.

fr.L: et un corps prit la route de Beth-Horôn, et un corps prit la route de la frontière qui domine la vallée de Tseboïm, du côté du désert.
fr.B: Un autre prit la route de Beth-Horôn, et un autre la route de la frontière qui domine la vallée de Tseboïm, du côté du désert.
fr.R: Un autre groupe est allé vers Beth-Horôn. Le troisième groupe est allé vers la frontière qui domine la vallée de Tseboïm, en face du désert.

vi.L: Một đội rẽ về hướng đường [đi] Bết-Hô-rôn, và một đội rẽ về hướng đường [đi] ranh giới nhìn xuống thung lũng Xê-bô-im, về phía hoang mạc.
vi.B: Đội khác rẽ về hướng đường đi Bết-Hô-rôn, còn đội kia rẽ về hướng đường đi đến vùng biên giới nhìn xuống thung lũng Xê-bô-im, về phía hoang mạc.
vi.R: Toán thứ hai đi về hướng Bết-Hô-rôn. Toán thứ ba đi về hướng vùng biên giới nhìn xuống thung lũng Xê-bô-im, hướng ra sa mạc.

decisions.choice: Beth-horon to the west; the Valley of Zeboim and the wilderness to the east
decisions.reason: Beth-horon lay west of Michmash, on the road down to the coastal plain (Joshua 10:10). The Valley of Zeboim seems to have run east toward the Jordan through the dry country there. With Ophrah to the north (verse 17), the raiders went out in three directions.

decisions.choice: the one company ... the one company: a first, a second and a third company
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names each company the same way, "the one company", as it lists them. The repeated phrase counts them off: a first, a second and a third.

decisions.choice: the desert
decisions.reason: The wilderness here is the dry, empty land toward the Jordan, so Readable calls it desert.

source.text: וְחָרָשׁ֙ לֹ֣א יִמָּצֵ֔א בְּכֹ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־אָמְר֣וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּ֚ן יַעֲשׂ֣וּ הָעִבְרִ֔ים חֶ֖רֶב א֥וֹ חֲנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And a craftsman not was found in all [the] land of Israel, for said [the] Philistines, lest make the Hebrews sword or spear.

en.L: And a smith was not found in all [the] land of Israel, for [the] Philistines said, "Lest the Hebrews make sword or spear."
en.B: No blacksmith could be found anywhere in Israel's land, for the Philistines had said, "The Hebrews must not make swords or spears."
en.R: At that time there were no blacksmiths anywhere in Israel. The Philistines had made sure of that. They said, "We do not want the Hebrews to make swords or spears for themselves."

es.L: Y no se hallaba herrero en toda [la] tierra de Israel, porque [los] filisteos decían: «No sea que los hebreos se hagan espada o lanza».
es.B: No se encontraba ningún herrero en toda la tierra de Israel, porque los filisteos habían dicho: «Los hebreos no deben fabricarse espadas ni lanzas».
es.R: En aquel tiempo no había herreros en ningún lugar de Israel. Los filisteos se habían asegurado de eso. Decían: «No queremos que los hebreos se hagan espadas ni lanzas».

fr.L: Et on ne trouvait pas de forgeron dans tout le pays d’Israël, car les Philistins avaient dit : « De peur que les Hébreux ne fassent épée ou lance. »
fr.B: On ne trouvait aucun forgeron dans tout le pays d’Israël, car les Philistins avaient dit : « Il ne faut pas que les Hébreux fabriquent des épées ou des lances. »
fr.R: À cette époque, il n’y avait aucun forgeron en Israël. Les Philistins y avaient veillé. Ils disaient : « Nous ne voulons pas que les Hébreux se fabriquent des épées ou des lances. »

vi.L: Trong khắp xứ Y-sơ-ra-ên không tìm thấy một thợ rèn nào, vì người Phi-li-tin đã nói: "Kẻo người Hê-bơ-rơ làm gươm hay giáo."
vi.B: Khắp xứ Y-sơ-ra-ên không có một thợ rèn nào, vì người Phi-li-tin đã nói: "Không được để người Hê-bơ-rơ làm gươm giáo."
vi.R: Thời ấy, khắp Y-sơ-ra-ên không có một thợ rèn nào. Người Phi-li-tin đã làm cho như vậy. Họ nói: "Chúng ta không muốn người Hê-bơ-rơ tự làm gươm giáo."

decisions.choice: a smith: a worker in metal
decisions.reason: The word means a craftsman of any kind, in wood, stone or metal. The swords and spears in the Philistines' words show that a metalworker is meant here.

decisions.choice: the Philistines kept metalworking out of Israel's hands
decisions.reason: The Philistines held the skill of working iron and kept it from the Israelites, so that they could not arm themselves. Verses 20-22 show the result: farmers had to go to the Philistines even to sharpen their tools.

decisions.choice: said: the Philistines (plural)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters have "he said" and the reading tradition has "they said". The sense is the same: it was the Philistines' policy.

decisions.choice: At that time; The Philistines had made sure of that
decisions.reason: Readable says what the verse implies: the lack of smiths was the Philistines' doing (m2).

source.text: וַיֵּרְד֥וּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים לִ֠לְטוֹשׁ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־מַחֲרַשְׁתּ֤וֹ וְאֶת־אֵתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־קַרְדֻּמּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת מַחֲרֵשָׁתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down all Israel [to] the Philistines to sharpen each his plowshare and his mattock and his axe and his plowshare.

en.L: And all Israel went down [to] the Philistines to sharpen each his plowshare and his mattock and his axe and his colter.
en.B: So all Israel had to go down to the Philistines to have their plowshares, mattocks, axes and colters sharpened.
en.R: So all the people of Israel had to go down to the Philistines to get their tools sharpened. They took their plow blades, hoes, axes and plow knives.

es.L: Y todo Israel bajaba [a] los filisteos para afilar cada uno su reja, y su azadón, y su hacha, y su cuchilla.
es.B: Así que todos los israelitas tenían que bajar a donde los filisteos para que les afilaran las rejas de arado, los azadones, las hachas y las cuchillas de arado.
es.R: Así que todo el pueblo de Israel tenía que bajar a donde los filisteos para que les afilaran sus herramientas. Llevaban las puntas de sus arados, sus azadones, sus hachas y las cuchillas de sus arados.

fr.L: Et tout Israël descendait chez les Philistins pour aiguiser chacun son soc, et sa pioche, et sa hache, et son coutre.
fr.B: Tout Israël devait donc descendre chez les Philistins pour faire aiguiser socs, pioches, haches et coutres.
fr.R: Alors tous les Israélites devaient descendre chez les Philistins pour faire aiguiser leurs outils. Ils apportaient leurs lames de charrue, leurs houes, leurs haches et leurs couteaux de charrue.

vi.L: Cả Y-sơ-ra-ên phải đi xuống đến người Phi-li-tin để mài lưỡi cày, cuốc, rìu và lưỡi cày khác của mình.
vi.B: Vì vậy cả Y-sơ-ra-ên phải đi xuống đến người Phi-li-tin để mài lưỡi cày, cuốc chim, rìu và dao cày.
vi.R: Vì vậy toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải đi xuống đến người Phi-li-tin để mài dụng cụ. Họ đem lưỡi cày, cuốc, rìu và dao cày đến đó.

decisions.choice: colter: another blade of the plow
decisions.reason: The fourth tool in the Hebrew list is written with the same letters as the first, "plowshare", but with different vowels. A list is unlikely to name the same tool twice, so it is taken as another kind of plow blade, such as the colter, the knife that cuts the soil ahead of the share. The ancient Greek translation has "sickle" here. The Hebrew text is followed, but the exact tool is not certain.

decisions.choice: plowshare, mattock, axe: iron-edged farm tools
decisions.reason: The plowshare is the blade that turns the soil; the mattock is a heavy hoe for breaking ground; the axe is for cutting wood. All need a smith to keep their edges.

decisions.choice: to sharpen: to have them sharpened
decisions.reason: The Israelites went to the Philistines for the work to be done, as verse 21 shows by giving the price.

decisions.choice: plow blades, hoes, plow knives
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the tools: "hoes" for mattocks, and "plow knives" for colters.

source.text: וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה הַפְּצִ֣ירָה פִ֗ים לַמַּֽחֲרֵשֹׁת֙ וְלָ֣אֵתִ֔ים וְלִשְׁלֹ֥שׁ קִלְּשׁ֖וֹן וּלְהַקַּרְדֻּמִּ֑ים וּלְהַצִּ֖יב הַדָּרְבָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And was the charge a pim for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and for three of fork and for the axes, and for setting the goad.

en.L: And the charge was a pim for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and a third [of a shekel] for the forks and for the axes, and for setting the goad.
en.B: The charge was {{units:about 1/4 ounce|a pim}} for plowshares and mattocks, and {{units:about 1/8 ounce|a third of a shekel}} for forks and axes and for fixing the points on ox goads.
en.R: The Philistines charged {{units:about 1/4 ounce|a pim}} of silver to sharpen a plow blade or a hoe. They charged {{units:about 1/8 ounce|a third of a shekel}} of silver to sharpen a fork or an axe, or to put a new point on an ox goad.

es.L: Y el precio era un pim por las rejas y por los azadones, y un tercio [de siclo] por los tridentes y por las hachas, y por enderezar la aguijada.
es.B: El precio era de {{units:unos 7,5 gramos|un pim}} por las rejas y los azadones, y de {{units:unos 4 gramos|un tercio de siclo}} por los tridentes, las hachas y por arreglar la punta de las aguijadas.
es.R: Los filisteos cobraban {{units:unos 7,5 gramos|un pim}} de plata por afilar la punta de un arado o un azadón. Cobraban {{units:unos 4 gramos|un tercio de siclo}} de plata por afilar un tridente o un hacha, o por ponerle punta nueva a una aguijada para bueyes.

fr.L: Et le prix était d’un pim pour les socs et pour les pioches, et d’un tiers [de sicle] pour les fourches et pour les haches, et pour redresser l’aiguillon.
fr.B: Le prix était de {{units:environ 7 grammes|un pim}} pour les socs et les pioches, et de {{units:environ 3,5 grammes|un tiers de sicle}} pour les fourches, les haches et pour remettre en place la pointe des aiguillons.
fr.R: Les Philistins faisaient payer {{units:environ 7 grammes|un pim}} d’argent pour aiguiser une lame de charrue ou une houe. Ils faisaient payer {{units:environ 3,5 grammes|un tiers de sicle}} d’argent pour aiguiser une fourche ou une hache, ou pour mettre une pointe neuve à un aiguillon.

vi.L: Giá là một phim cho lưỡi cày và cuốc, và một phần ba [siếc-lơ] cho chĩa và rìu, và cho việc gắn mũi đót.
vi.B: Giá mài là {{units:khoảng 8 gam bạc|một phim}} cho lưỡi cày và cuốc chim, và {{units:khoảng 4 gam bạc|một phần ba siếc-lơ}} cho chĩa, rìu và việc sửa mũi gậy đót bò.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin đòi {{units:khoảng 8 gam|một phim}} bạc để mài một lưỡi cày hay một cái cuốc. Họ đòi {{units:khoảng 4 gam|một phần ba siếc-lơ}} bạc để mài một cái chĩa hay một cái rìu, hoặc để gắn mũi mới cho cây gậy đót bò.

decisions.choice: pim: a weight of about two-thirds of a shekel
decisions.reason: The word appears only here in the Bible, and its meaning was long unknown. Small stone weights inscribed with this word have since been found in Israel. They weigh about two-thirds of a shekel, a little over a quarter of an ounce. The charge was paid in silver by weight.

decisions.choice: a third of a shekel for the forks
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "for three" beside a rare word for a fork. Read with the price before it, "three" is taken as a third of a shekel, a second, lower charge. Another reading takes the words as "three-pronged forks", with no second price.

decisions.choice: the charge: the price for sharpening
decisions.reason: This word too is found only here. It seems to mean the fee the Philistine smiths charged. The point of the verse is that Israel depended on its enemies and paid them for every edge.

decisions.choice: setting the goad: fitting or straightening the metal point of an ox goad
decisions.reason: A goad was a long stick with a sharp point used to drive oxen (Judges 3:31). It too needed a smith's work.

decisions.choice: about 1/4 ounce; about 1/8 ounce
decisions.reason: A shekel is about 2/5 ounce, so two-thirds of a shekel is a little over 1/4 ounce and a third of a shekel a little over 1/8 ounce. The original units are the alternative.

decisions.choice: The Philistines charged ... of silver to sharpen
decisions.reason: Readable says who charged, what was paid and what the payment was for, in line with m1 and m3.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 8 gam" and "khoảng 4 gam" by default, "một phim" and "một phần ba siếc-lơ" with the Measures setting; Literal keeps the original weights
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses metric measures by default: a pim is about two-thirds of a shekel (meaning decision) and a shekel 11.5 g (Samuel terms note).

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ בְּי֣וֹם מִלְחֶ֔מֶת וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א חֶ֤רֶב וַחֲנִית֙ בְּיַ֣ד כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶת־שָׁא֖וּל וְאֶת־יוֹנָתָ֑ן וַתִּמָּצֵ֣א לְשָׁא֔וּל וּלְיוֹנָתָ֖ן בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on [the] day of battle, and not was found sword or spear in [the] hand of all the people that [were] with Saul and with Jonathan; and was found for Saul and for Jonathan his son.

en.L: And it was on [the] day of battle, and sword or spear was not found in [the] hand of any of the people who [were] with Saul and with Jonathan; but [one] was found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.
en.B: So on the day of battle, not one of the soldiers with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or a spear in hand; only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.
en.R: So when the day of battle came, none of the soldiers with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or a spear. Only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.

es.L: Y sucedió que el día de la batalla no se halló espada ni lanza en [la] mano de nadie del pueblo que [estaba] con Saúl y con Jonatán; pero se halló [una] con Saúl y con Jonatán su hijo.
es.B: Así que el día de la batalla ninguno de los soldados que estaban con Saúl y Jonatán tenía en la mano espada ni lanza; solo Saúl y su hijo Jonatán las tenían.
es.R: Por eso, cuando llegó el día de la batalla, ninguno de los soldados de Saúl y de Jonatán tenía espada ni lanza. Solo Saúl y su hijo Jonatán tenían armas.

fr.L: Et il arriva, au jour du combat, qu’on ne trouva ni épée ni lance dans la main de tout le peuple qui [était] avec Saül et avec Jonathan ; mais il s’en trouva pour Saül et pour Jonathan son fils.
fr.B: Le jour du combat, aucun des soldats qui étaient avec Saül et Jonathan n’avait d’épée ni de lance en main ; seuls Saül et son fils Jonathan en avaient.
fr.R: Alors, quand le jour du combat est arrivé, aucun des soldats de Saül et de Jonathan n’avait d’épée ou de lance. Seuls Saül et son fils Jonathan avaient des armes.

vi.L: Vào ngày giao chiến, không tìm thấy gươm hay giáo trong tay bất cứ ai trong dân chúng ở với Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than; nhưng Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai ông thì có.
vi.B: Vì vậy vào ngày giao chiến, không một người lính nào theo Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than có gươm hay giáo trong tay; chỉ Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than con trai ông là có.
vi.R: Vì vậy, khi ngày giao chiến đến, không một người lính nào theo Sau-lơ và Giô-na-than có gươm hay giáo. Chỉ có Sau-lơ và con trai ông là Giô-na-than có vũ khí.

decisions.choice: the day of battle: the fighting about to be told in chapter 14
decisions.reason: The verse looks ahead to the battle at Michmash. Israel's army goes into it with farm tools, not proper weapons.

decisions.choice: only Saul and Jonathan were armed: victory will not come by weapons
decisions.reason: The writer stresses how weak Israel was, which sets up chapter 14, where the LORD gives the victory through Jonathan and his armor-bearer (14:6, 23). The same point is made later with David and Goliath (17:47).

decisions.choice: soldiers
decisions.reason: "The people" with Saul and Jonathan are his fighting men, so Balanced and Readable call them soldiers.

en.L: And the garrison of [the] Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.
en.B: Now the Philistine garrison had moved out to the pass at Michmash.
en.R: Meanwhile, a group of Philistine soldiers had gone out to guard the pass at Michmash.

es.B: La guarnición filistea se había desplazado al paso de Micmas.
es.R: Mientras tanto, un grupo de soldados filisteos había salido a vigilar el paso de Micmas.

fr.L: Et le poste des Philistins sortit vers le passage de Mikmash.
fr.B: Or le poste des Philistins s’était avancé jusqu’au passage de Mikmash.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, un groupe de soldats philistins était parti garder le passage de Mikmash.

vi.L: Đồn binh Phi-li-tin kéo ra đến đèo Mích-ma.
vi.B: Bấy giờ đồn binh Phi-li-tin đã kéo ra đèo Mích-ma.
vi.R: Trong khi đó, một toán quân Phi-li-tin đã kéo ra canh giữ đèo Mích-ma.

decisions.choice: garrison: an outpost of soldiers
decisions.reason: The word is related to the one for the Philistine post in verse 3. It names a body of troops stationed at a place to hold it.

decisions.choice: the pass of Michmash: the crossing of the ravine between Michmash and Geba
decisions.reason: The deep valley between the two camps could be crossed at a few places only. The Philistines put a post at the crossing, and Jonathan will climb up to it in 14:4-13.

decisions.choice: to guard
decisions.reason: Readable says why the soldiers went to the pass (m2).
